I've found that the main jet pretty much always gets fowled up, likely with rubber and plastic which is eaten away by the gasoline and deposited there. If you have an old engine with adjustable jet, you can get away by just enriching the mix by loosening the jet; if you have a carb which is good for the environment so much so that it needs continuous maintenance to be clean (aka nonadjustable jet), you need to disassemble it and clean any buildup off.

Another option if you aren't savvy and the engine can kinda run say on half choke is to fill the tank up with the recommended amount of fuel system cleaner and run it for a while, listening for when you can hear the engine sputtering a little bit, then open the choke up slightly and let it continue running. Not fuel efficient and not always an option but it can be done.
